changes.text: Practice pages can now let you know when an update is ready and show what changed after reloading.
Update checks now handle double-digit release numbers and brief deployment cache delays reliably.
Speaking practice now explains what Enter will do at each step and lets you press R to record the answer again.
Cloud sync status now sits beneath the header navigation on every page so it is easier to distinguish from page links.
Update notices and changelogs now match the trainer's colors, typography, buttons, and visual depth.
A new visual lesson teaches pointing words, prices, shopping, ownership, locations, restaurant ordering, and classroom survival phrases through connected situations.
Long update histories now use one clean scrollbar in the changelog.
Numbers practice now lets you say a displayed number in Japanese. Correct speech is accepted automatically, while a mismatch stays unscored so you can retry with R or type in Japanese or romaji.
Pattern mastery can now be expanded when needed and stays compact while you practice.
Correct spoken vocabulary answers are now accepted automatically. A mismatch stays unscored so you can retry with R or type your answer.
The Submit answer button now appears only when typing, since correct speech is accepted automatically and mismatched speech remains available to retry.
Japanese suffixes now use short, natural carrier expressions to give speech recognition enough context while regular vocabulary remains an isolated word check.
Speech diagnostics can now collect local, audio-free evidence from retry chains that end with a correct answer, with controls to review, copy, or clear it.
Practice scope now offers guided study, quick lesson selections, and any custom combination of curriculum topics in one focused picker.
Curriculum topics now open a searchable word browser with topic statistics, individual learning status and accuracy, pronunciation, and a direct practice shortcut.
Scrollable panels and native controls now consistently use the app’s dark appearance.
Topic word lists can now be sorted by curriculum order, Japanese text, or accuracy, while unpractised words stay out of the way of accuracy rankings.
Every submitted vocabulary answer now includes a natural example sentence, an English translation, and separate sentence pronunciation playback.
Practice all 802 official JLPT N5 vocabulary entries by topic, each with a kana-only example sentence, alongside the separate Genki II Course track.
Words shared between tracks now keep one learning history, and the former Practical extras vocabulary has moved into JLPT N5.
Choose the Genki II Course or JLPT N5 first, then quickly practise a whole track or open a focused, searchable topic selector.
Advanced topic mixing remains available without crowding the most common study choices.
Guided JLPT N5 practice now introduces vocabulary one topic at a time while keeping earlier N5 words available for review.
Recommendation labels now sit quietly beside each guided track instead of competing with the practice choice.
The curriculum now follows the selected vocabulary track, while combined scopes keep Genki II and JLPT N5 clearly grouped.
Session controls now gently point new learners toward practice scope until they have changed it three times.
The practice-scope hint now waits briefly after Session controls opens, making the guidance feel calmer and easier to notice.
The Genki II Course now includes all 118 vocabulary entries from Lessons 3 and 4, organised into focused topics with kana-only example sentences.
Lesson 3 and Lesson 4 can now be selected directly as practice scopes, while words shared with JLPT N5 keep one learning history.
Learn 104 core N5 preparation kanji in small stages with answer-safe practice choices, highlighted example sentences, adaptive review, checkpoints, and a searchable progress map.
Kanji practice now follows one JLPT N5 journey, reveals every choice’s learning details after answering, offers automatic pronunciation, and uses polished session controls.
Kanji questions now use the full practice area, while the complete JLPT N5 journey remains available in a compact section below.
Each kanji stage now opens a focused overview with its theme, progress, and characters, with direct access to complete kanji details.
Kanji map search and status filters now match the polished controls used throughout the lessons.

The new-kanji pace slider now counts successful recall reviews, while a three-kanji learning buffer and direction-specific mistake checks prevent new material from outrunning recall. Established kanji return on a longer time-based schedule.
Review now focuses on learned kanji, while Practice lets you work through all 120 kanji, your learned set, or any combination of curriculum groups with persistent coverage progress.
Kanji knowledge now carries between Practice and Learn. Familiar characters receive a quick check, while only accurate, varied, and delayed Practice evidence can count toward the guided journey.
The Genki II Course now includes all 99 vocabulary entries from Lessons 5 and 6, organised into focused topics with kana-only example sentences.
Lesson 5 and Lesson 6 can now be selected directly as practice scopes, while words shared with JLPT N5 keep one learning history.
Guided Lesson 2 progress now syncs between signed-in devices instead of remaining queued in the browser.

Session controls now explain exactly which directions Mixed practice uses and keep control arrows comfortably aligned. The dashboard and scope picker show accuracy for selected lessons and topics, with session results kept as supporting context.
English-to-Japanese questions now reveal the pronunciation and meaning of every answer choice after you respond.

releases.title: Sentence structure help in vocabulary practice

changes.text: Genki Lesson 3 examples now include an optional sentence breakdown with contextual meanings, particle roles, and a concise explanation of the overall structure.
Lesson 3 sentence breakdowns now explain how each particle works in its particular sentence, including special pronunciations, and remember whether you prefer breakdowns open or closed.
Lesson 3 examples now arrange Japanese phrases, particles, and their contextual meanings into clear visual chunks, matching the familiar learning style used in Kana Mix.
Vocabulary answer choices now use clean, concise meanings instead of unfinished source notes, merged examples, or corrupted fragments.
Listening questions no longer replay automatically after you answer. The prompt and manual replay controls remain available, while automatic pronunciation continues for other directions.
The vocabulary speech setting now keeps its explanation grouped with the toggle and aligns voice management cleanly beside it.
Revealed English-to-Japanese choices now keep the Japanese expression prominent while placing its pronunciation and meaning together on a compact second line.
Vocabulary practice now gently brings revealed feedback into view and returns to the next question when needed, while avoiding unnecessary movement when the relevant content is already visible.
When the completed vocabulary practice card fits on screen, answer review now keeps the entire card visible; smaller screens continue to prioritize the revealed feedback.
